name: Azure REST API Guidelines
description: Style rules based on Microsoft Azure REST API Guidelines

rules.title: Use api-version query parameter
rules.rationale: Azure APIs must use the api-version query parameter for versioning.

rules.title: Version format YYYY-MM-DD
rules.rationale: Azure API versions must use YYYY-MM-DD format.

judge.prompt: Check if the API version parameters use YYYY-MM-DD format (e.g., 2024-01-15). Look at examples, descriptions, and any version-related fields.

rules.title: Use lowercase paths
rules.rationale: Azure API paths must be lowercase for consistency.

rules.title: Use plural resource names
rules.rationale: Collection resources should use plural names.

judge.prompt: Check if resource collection paths use plural nouns (users, not user). Individual resources accessed by ID are fine as children of plural collections.

rules.title: Use camelCase for path parameters
rules.rationale: Path parameters should use camelCase.

rules.title: Avoid deep nesting
rules.rationale: Paths should not exceed 5 segments for readability.

judge.prompt: Check if any paths have more than 5 segments (excluding the version). Deep nesting makes APIs harder to use.

rules.title: GET must not have request body
rules.rationale: GET requests must not have a request body per HTTP specification.

rules.title: DELETE should return 204
rules.rationale: Successful DELETE operations should return 204 No Content.

rules.title: POST should return 201 for creation
rules.rationale: POST operations that create resources should return 201 Created.

rules.title: Use camelCase for property names
rules.rationale: JSON property names must use camelCase.

rules.title: Use standard date-time format
rules.rationale: Date-time values must use ISO 8601 format.

judge.prompt: Check if date and time properties use string type with format 'date-time' (ISO 8601). Look for properties with names like 'createdAt', 'updatedAt', 'timestamp', etc.

rules.title: Use string for IDs
rules.rationale: Resource IDs should be strings to support various ID formats including GUIDs.

judge.prompt: Check if resource ID properties (id, resourceId, etc.) are typed as string rather than integer. Azure typically uses GUIDs.

rules.title: Use standard error format
rules.rationale: Error responses must follow Azure error format with code, message, and optional target/details.

judge.prompt: Check if error responses (4xx, 5xx) use Azure error format: {"error": {"code": "string", "message": "string", "target": "string", "details": []}}

rules.title: Include error code
rules.rationale: Error responses must include a machine-readable error code.

judge.prompt: Check if error response schemas include a 'code' property for machine-readable error identification.

rules.title: Use nextLink for pagination
rules.rationale: Collection responses should use nextLink for pagination continuation.

judge.prompt: Check if collection responses include a 'nextLink' property for pagination. Collections should return {"value": [...], "nextLink": "url"}

rules.title: Support $top and $skip
rules.rationale: Collection endpoints should support $top and $skip query parameters.

judge.prompt: Check if collection (list) endpoints support $top and $skip query parameters for pagination control.

rules.title: Use Location header for LRO
rules.rationale: Long-running operations should return 202 Accepted with Location header.

judge.prompt: Check if operations that may take a long time (create, update complex resources) return 202 Accepted with a Location header for polling.

rules.title: Include Retry-After header
rules.rationale: 202 responses should include Retry-After header.

judge.prompt: Check if 202 Accepted responses document Retry-After header in the response headers.

rules.title: Use consistent naming patterns
rules.rationale: Similar concepts should use consistent naming across the API.

judge.prompt: Check for consistent naming patterns. For example, if some schemas use 'createdDateTime' and others use 'createdAt', that's inconsistent.

rules.title: Avoid abbreviations
rules.rationale: Use full words instead of abbreviations for clarity.

judge.prompt: Check if property and schema names avoid unnecessary abbreviations. 'configuration' is better than 'config', 'identifier' better than 'id' (though 'id' is acceptable).

rules.title: Define security scheme
rules.rationale: API must define authentication requirements.

rules.title: Apply security globally
rules.rationale: Security should be applied at the API level.

rules.title: Use OAuth2 or Azure AD
rules.rationale: Azure APIs should use OAuth2 with Azure AD.

judge.prompt: Check if the security scheme uses OAuth2 (preferably with Azure AD flows). API key authentication alone is not recommended.
